23 A rubber cord hangs from a rigid support. A weight attached to its lower end is gradually
increased from zero, and then gradually reduced to zero.
force
stretching
rubber
cord
contraction
weight
extension
0
0
The force–extension curve for contraction is below the force–extension curve for stretching.
What does the shaded area between the curves represent?
A
the elastic potential energy stored in the rubber cord
B
the thermal energy dissipated in the rubber cord
C
the work done by the rubber cord during contraction
D
the work done on the rubber cord during stretching

hints: Notice the force-extension graph has an upper stretching curve and a lower contraction curve enclosing a shaded loop.
Recall that area under a $force$ against $extension$ graph represents work done, with units of $\text{J}$.
Compare the larger work input under the stretching curve with the smaller work output under the contraction curve to see what the difference must represent.
walkthrough: Identify the two areas: the area under the upper stretching curve from $0$ to maximum extension is the work done on the cord, given by $W = \int F dx$.
Identify the area under the lower contraction curve from maximum extension back to $0$ is the useful work done by the cord as it shortens.
Subtract the two: because the contraction curve lies below the stretching curve, work recovered is less than work supplied.
The missing energy is not returned as mechanical work but causes internal friction in the rubber, warming it.
Therefore the shaded loop area between the curves equals work lost as heat. This is option B.

A.explanation: Elastic potential energy stored would be the area under the contraction curve that is returned, not the difference between the two curves.

B.explanation: The loop area is the net work lost as work done on stretching exceeds work recovered on contraction, dissipated as thermal energy in the rubber.

C.explanation: Work done by the cord during contraction is the full area under the lower contraction curve to the extension axis, not just the thin loop between curves.

D.explanation: Work done on the cord during stretching is the full area under the upper stretching curve to the extension axis, not just the thin loop between curves.
